stair-treads/siesta-key.h1: Stair Tread Installation on Siesta Key, FL
stair-treads/siesta-key.lede: Stair tread installation on Siesta Key is a small, specific slice of our work, limited mostly to Sanderling Club's two-story homes and a handful of townhome-style condos.
stair-treads/siesta-key.capsule: Stair tread installation is a small share of our Siesta Key work, since most of the island's condo units are single-level and stairs only come up in Sanderling Club's two-story homes and the handful of townhome-style buildings elsewhere. Typical 2026 installed ranges run $55 to $220 per tread depending on material, plus $25 to $65 per riser. A typical 14-tread staircase finishes in one to two days.
stair-treads/siesta-key.body_html:
Most flooring on Siesta Key never touches a staircase. The island's condo stock, more than 85 named associations, is almost entirely single-level living, units stacked vertically inside a building rather than spread across two floors within a single unit, so stair tread work here is a small, specific slice of our business rather than a routine add-on to a flooring job.

Where it does come up is Sanderling Club, the gated enclave described on our Siesta Key area page, toward the island's south end, where a two-story layout is common enough that we get a steady handful of staircase jobs each year, plus the scattered townhome-style condo buildings elsewhere on the island that stack two floors within one unit rather than one floor per unit. A 14-tread straight staircase connecting a Sanderling Club home's main level to a second-floor primary suite is a common request: solid or engineered hardwood treads to match new flooring installed above and below, or LVP treads when the rest of the house is going that direction instead.

Material choice usually follows whatever floor is going in on both levels rather than standing alone, since a mismatched tread on an otherwise matched floor reads as an afterthought. Engineered hardwood treads hold up better than solid on a stairwell that catches direct sun through a window, a detail worth flagging before ordering material given how much of the island's light comes off open water. Our post on putting vinyl plank flooring on stairs covers the nosing and adhesive details for anyone leaning toward LVP treads instead of wood.

Condo stairwells, when they exist, add their own wrinkle: association rules that govern flooring sound ratings inside a unit sometimes extend to interior stairs too, so we confirm the specific building's flooring approval requirements, checked against the condo flooring approval checklist, before quoting tread material for a townhome-style unit rather than assuming the same rule that applies to a single-family Sanderling Club stairwell. Nosing profile is worth deciding early too, since a rounded bullnose reads differently against wide-plank flooring than the squared edge some homeowners prefer for a more modern stair.
stair-treads/siesta-key.cost_html:
A 14-tread straight staircase in engineered hardwood treads runs $110-$180 per tread installed, or $1,540-$2,520 for the full run, typical 2026 range; 13 matching risers add $325-$845 more depending on finish. Solid hardwood treads push the per-tread price to $130-$220, or $1,820-$3,080 for the same 14 treads, and LVP treads bring it down to $65-$105 per tread, or $910-$1,470 total, for homeowners matching a vinyl floor above and below.

Laminate treads are the least common request on Siesta Key given the island's humidity, running $55-$85 per tread when we do install them. Our stair treads cost guide breaks down pricing for every material combination.

faqs.q: Do Siesta Key condos have stairs inside the unit?
faqs.a: Almost never. The island's condo stock is overwhelmingly single-level units stacked inside a building, so interior stair tread work is mostly limited to Sanderling Club's two-story single-family homes and a handful of townhome-style buildings.

faqs.q: What stair tread material holds up best on Siesta Key?
faqs.a: Engineered hardwood generally outlasts solid wood on a stairwell that catches direct sun through a window, common in homes with open water views, since engineered's layered construction resists the seasonal movement better.

faqs.q: Do Siesta Key condo associations regulate interior stairs?
faqs.a: Some townhome-style buildings extend the same sound-rating rules that apply to floors to interior stairs, so we check the specific association's requirements before quoting tread material for anything other than a single-family Sanderling Club home.
